title: CQL: Fix metadata offset desynchronization for NULL and empty compound types
description:
The CQL dissector used hardcoded byte offsets (+2, +4) to skip metadata
for NULL values and empty collections (LIST, MAP, SET).  This only worked
for simple element types; compound types such as nested collections, UDTs,
tuples, and custom types have variable-length metadata descriptors, so the
hardcoded skips caused the metadata cursor to go out of sync, corrupting
dissection of all subsequent columns in the row.

Add a recursive skip_metadata_type() function that mirrors parse_option()
to correctly walk a complete type descriptor tree, and use it everywhere
metadata needs to be advanced without consuming row data:

- NULL column values (bytes_length == -1)
- "Not set" column values (bytes_length == -2, CQL protocol v4+)
- Invalid negative length values (flagged with expert info)
- Empty LIST, MAP, and SET collections (size == 0)

AI-assisted: Yes, OpenCode with Claude Opus 4.6. But I found the issue, reviewed the fix
and used a capture that failed before and passed after.

Signed-off-by: Yaniv Kaul <mykaul@gmail.com>
